title: Seatrium secures S$1.7 billion in new contracts this year, expects significantly higher underlying net profit in FY2026
text:
Seatrium secures S$1.7 billion in new contracts this year, expects higher FY2026 net profit | Lianhe Zaobao 
 Singapore International China Business Opinion Lifestyle Entertainment Search Tobby Siew Published / 19 Nov 2026 08:58 S M L XL Seatrium secures S$1.7 billion in new contracts this year, expects significantly higher underlying net profit in FY2026
 AI-translated article with transliterated names. Read original Chinese article here. 
 As of 30 September this year, Seatrium’s net order book stood at S$12.2 billion across 35 projects, providing revenue visibility through to 2033. （File picture） Seatrium has secured S$1.7 billion worth of new contracts so far this year and expects underlying net profit for the 2026 financial year to be significantly higher than in FY2025. 
 In a business update released before the market opened on Thursday (19 November), Seatrium said the S$1.7 billion in new contracts included a floating storage regasification unit conversion project and a floating production storage and offloading vessel integration project. 
 As of 30 September this year, Seatrium’s net order book stood at S$12.2 billion across 35 projects, providing revenue visibility through to 2033. 
 Seatrium also said its operating performance remained stable, with revenue holding steady and gross margins improving from the first half. “The gross margin expansion was supported by improving project margin mix, continued cost discipline and progressive cost savings associated with ongoing non-core divestments.” 
 The group said completed divestments were helping it save more than S$50 million in costs annually. 
 Chief executive Chris Ong said Seatrium was maintaining strong execution and continuing to improve gross margins as it worked to build a more resilient and profitable company. 
 Ong also said the group’s order-winning momentum had accelerated in recent weeks, reflecting strong underlying market demand. “Alongside steady improvements in margins, we are committed and well-positioned to drive long-term total shareholder returns.” 
 Seatrium shares fell 0.58% to S$1.71 on Wednesday.
